proposed_comments.title: Keep unit-test sources out of the production DLL
proposed_comments.body:
### Keep unit-test sources out of the production DLL

**Severity:** `high`

`UnitTests\MonitorTopologyTests.cpp` is listed in the production `CursorWrap.vcxproj`, so the production project attempts to compile the CppUnitTest source. This causes the exact upstream CursorWrap build to fail with `C1010` while looking for the precompiled header and would incorrectly place test code in the production build. Remove this compile entry; the file is already owned by `CursorWrapUnitTests.vcxproj`.

**Verification:** Build both CursorWrap projects and run `CursorWrap.UnitTests`.

confidence.rationale: The exact upstream build fails at this production compile entry, and removing it is part of the candidate that builds and passes all focused tests.

proposed_comments.title: Do not wrap sideways from a suppressed top corner
proposed_comments.body:
### Do not wrap sideways from a suppressed top corner

**Severity:** `high`

When the top edge is suppressed at a global-top monitor corner, the current code removes only the `Top` candidate and then allows the remaining `Left` or `Right` candidate to win. Upward or unknown movement can therefore wrap sideways instead of being blocked at the RDP connection-bar edge.

Handle this condition before candidate selection: return no edge for vertical-dominant or unknown movement, while preserving side wrapping for horizontal movement. Add corner-focused regression coverage.

confidence.rationale: The candidate-selection flow directly permits the sideways fallback, and the validated correction handles the direction before selecting an edge.

proposed_comments.title: Add regression coverage for suppressed top corners
proposed_comments.body:
### Add regression coverage for suppressed top corners

**Severity:** `medium`

The current tests verify ordinary top suppression and unaffected horizontal edges, but not the corner fallback that can wrap upward movement sideways. Add a test covering a global-top corner with upward movement and unknown direction, both of which must return no edge, plus horizontal movement, which must still select the side edge.

**Verification:** Run the focused CursorWrap unit-test assembly and confirm all corner-direction cases pass.

confidence.rationale: The missing branch is observable at a top corner and is covered by the validated candidate's regression test.

proposed_comments.title: Synchronize the live RDP setting
proposed_comments.body:
### Synchronize the live RDP setting

**Severity:** `high`

The settings runner thread writes `m_suppressTopEdgeWrapInRemoteSession` while `MouseHookProc` reads it on a separate hook thread. Keeping this as a plain `bool` creates a C++ data race when the setting changes while Cursor Wrap is active.

Store it as `std::atomic_bool` and use a relaxed load in the hook path. Rebuild CursorWrap and rerun the focused unit tests.

confidence.rationale: The setting is written and read by distinct live threads without synchronization; the validated candidate uses an atomic value.
